A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSeq-JEPA work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original DSeq-JEPA benchmark results, component and ordering ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds an inverse-order result, saliency-agreement evidence, and a three-seed evaluation.

M1.justification: The encoders, saliency-based region selection, probabilistic curriculum, sequential predictor, and Huber objective remain unchanged. Specifying the small-component cutoff clarifies an existing filtering step rather than establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K, iNaturalist21, CUB, Stanford Cars, MS-COCO, ADE20K, and CLEVR for the same tasks. The added controls and saliency diagnostics do not introduce distinct dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds an inverse-order comparator. Table 1 also supplies I-JEPA comparisons for the ViT-H/16 fine-grained settings previously left blank. Other external baseline families remain unchanged; newly cited DMT-JEPA is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v4 introduces an inverse-order control and a Top-20 patch IoU measurement. Table 1 reclassifies LeJEPA from without to with view augmentations, revising the reported setting without establishing a rerun. Existing benchmark protocols otherwise match.

E4.justification: v4 adds an inverse-order ablation testing prediction direction and a visual/quantitative comparison of CLS and Grad-CAM saliency. The region-count sensitivity study already appears in v2 Appendix A.2/Table 9 and is merely moved into Section 4.3.

E5.justification: Unlike v2, v4 Section 4.2 explicitly reports repetition with three random seeds and 73.8 ± 0.4 accuracy for ImageNet ViT-B/16. This adds uncertainty reporting for one setting, although the statistic represented by ± is not defined.

E6.justification: Existing proposed-method benchmark scores are retained. Additions include I-JEPA ViT-H fine-grained scores of 38.9/67.2/67.7, inverse-order accuracy of 71.3, saliency IoU of 0.41, and the three-seed summary of 73.8 ± 0.4. Table 1's newly added overall-gain annotation of +1.5 conflicts with its displayed averages: 69.7 minus 68.4 equals 1.3.

T1.justification: The mathematical content of Equations 1–8 and Algorithm 1 is retained. No theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive formal assumption is added; the newly specified filtering cutoff is an implementation detail.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about discriminative region prioritization, sequential latent prediction, their synergy, and transfer improvements. Additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations that prediction direction matters, CLS saliency agrees with Grad-CAM, and the repeated ImageNet result is stable across runs. It removes the footnote defending improvement magnitudes; the existing curriculum, synergy, and region-count interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix A.1 newly specify removal of components with |Rk| < 0.15hw. The advertised access link changes from a GitHub repository to a project website. Other architecture, optimization, hardware, and downstream implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds DMT-JEPA and distinguishes its modification of latent targets from DSeq-JEPA's selection and ordering. The iNaturalist citation changes from the 2021 competition resource to the 2018 dataset paper, while the evaluated dataset remains described as iNaturalist21.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized prose and caption edits, moves region-count sensitivity into the main ablations, renames Appendix A.2, and adds acknowledgements, affiliations, and equal-contribution information. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds the saliency comparison Figure 5 and an inverse-order column in Table 5, restyles Figure 4, and replaces appendix Table 9 with main-text prose retaining its values. Figures and tables are rearranged, LeJEPA is regrouped, and page margins expand.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly strengthens empirical support through the inverse-order control, saliency comparison, three-seed reporting, and missing ViT-H baseline results, while clarifying the filtering cutoff. These incremental benefits outweigh the new Table 1 arithmetic inconsistency (+1.5 instead of +1.3). Uncertainty reporting remains limited to one configuration, and the central scientific contribution is unchanged.
